<reflection>
From the first experiment, many mechanisms fit the data almost equally well (negative log-likelihood values around -23.2), with M7 being slightly better but not significantly so. M3 fits less well (NLL ≈ -16.8), and M4 and M5 are clearly ruled out (positive NLL). The aim of the first experiment was to gather baseline kinetic data, which was achieved. Now, we need to design an experiment to discriminate among the remaining plausible mechanisms.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
By lowering the catalyst concentration by a factor of 10 (from 0.01 to 0.001) while keeping substrate moderate and no initial product, we probe the dependence of the reaction rate on catalyst concentration. Mechanisms that involve catalyst dimerization (e.g., M2, M3, M19) predict a different scaling (e.g., quadratic at low catalyst) compared to the linear scaling in simple Michaelis-Menten (M1). Inactivation mechanisms that are bimolecular in catalyst (e.g., M13, M18, M19) would show reduced inactivation at lower catalyst concentration, altering the time profile. This experiment avoids extreme conditions that might saturate or deplete the system and is informative for distinguishing among many mechanisms simultaneously, as it tests for catalyst-catalyst interactions and catalyst concentration dependencies that vary across the candidate set.
</hypothesis>
